svg.text: A model-free null on inverted real curves: the AR(1) significance gate runs hot
Every number re-derived from the committed P75 report; positive controls; nothing gated, anchored or claimed (discoveryClaim = false).
P75 | Is the significance gate honest?
Fraction of planet-free noise dips the gate calls significant (FAP<0.05).
AR(1)-model gate
model-free block
nominal target
AR(1) signs off 148/200 = 74% noise dips -- 15x the 5% it claims.
Of those, the model-free null rejects 86; mean FAP delta (block-AR1) +0.187.
GATE-OPTIMISTIC-ON-REAL-NOISE - AR(1) understates real tails.
The null | pure noise by design
Invert a real curve, mask every catalogued planet, keep a positive dip.
planet-free noise dips
quiet hosts (rho<=0.2)
1. flux -> 2*median - flux: every transit becomes a bump, so the curve
holds no real dip for a detector to find.
2. mask each catalogued planet (ground-truth ephemeris, widened) to drop
the mirrored bumps; single sector keeps the ephemeris exact.
3. keep only a POSITIVE transit-like residual dip - what's left is noise.
This is the model-free recalibration P69 asked for, on real photometry.
Measured, not gated
The AR(1) null is the gate's own significance yardstick; a 74% false-alarm rate on pure noise says it runs
hot. This study only QUANTIFIES that - it changes no threshold, gates nothing, and touches no critic or money path.
safeToGate = false; discoveryClaim = false; every number is re-derived from the committed P75 report.
